ir.title: Reading absorption bands
ir.provenance: Synthetic teaching data generated for SpectraSuite. Two Gaussian dips on a constant transmission background.
steps: Open the example and confirm the descending wavenumber axis and the % transmittance scale.
Locate the two downward bands near 2920 and 1720 cm⁻¹. In Analyze, hover over the tools to find the valley selection tool.
Compare the band positions in the raw trace. Confirm the signal representation before comparing band intensities or areas.
ir.expected: Transmittance minima near 1720 and 2920 cm⁻¹ on a descending wavenumber axis.
ir.caption: Reference plot from the bundled synthetic dataset.

ir.title: Measured polystyrene sheet
ir.provenance: Fabio Corradini, uFTIR reference data. Agilent Cary 620 microscope, transmission, 4× objective, 8 cm⁻¹ resolution, 8 sample scans and 16 background scans. One measured pixel (24, 72). Converted from the deposited absorbance with %T = 100 × 10⁻ᴬ. All 572 points are retained.
ir.license: GPL-3.0 (upstream uFTIR). Source vector archive and license are bundled in docs/learn/sources.
ir.expected: A strong trough near 1601 cm⁻¹ and several near-zero troughs between about 2860 and 3050 cm⁻¹. Several source absorbance values reach exactly 8, so band depths in those regions are unreliable.
steps: Open the example and turn smoothing off to compare with the reference plot. Confirm the descending wavenumber axis and the percent transmittance scale.
Zoom around 1600 cm⁻¹. Use the Data table to locate the lowest transmittance in that local region. Compare with the nominal band near 1601 cm⁻¹.

Inspect the near-zero transmittance region around the C–H bands. The deposited values reach a common absorbance ceiling there. Practice comparing positions and avoid quantitative peak heights or areas in those troughs.
ir.caption: Measured pixel spectrum converted from absorbance to percent transmittance. No smoothing or baseline correction was applied.

xrd.title: Measuring diffraction peak width
xrd.provenance: Synthetic teaching data generated for SpectraSuite. Two Gaussian peaks on a constant intensity background.
steps: Locate the peak near 32° in 2θ.
Use Analyze to find the peak and check Show FWHM and grain size. Disable smoothing for comparison with the nominal raw width.
Compare the position and width with the library. Follow the Scherrer guide to see how the width enters a size estimate.
xrd.expected: Peaks near 32° and 46°. The first raw peak has a nominal FWHM of about 1.18° in 2θ.
xrd.caption: Reference plot from the bundled synthetic dataset.

xrd.title: Measured LaB₆ reference powder
xrd.provenance: NIST SRM 660c lanthanum hexaboride pattern distributed in the Advanced Photon Source GSAS-II tutorial, Create Instrument Parameter File. The tutorial identifies Cu Kα lab data. All 8,378 original counts were retained and the angle grid was reconstructed from the GSAS bank header.
xrd.license: GSAS-II tutorial repository redistribution notice. The upstream data and full notice are bundled in docs/learn/sources.
xrd.expected: Strong reflections near 21.28°, 30.32° and 37.37° 2θ. At higher angles, a close pair near 67.49° and 67.67° illustrates why a single-peak width can be misleading.
steps: Open the example and turn smoothing off. Zoom near 30.3° and compare the sampled peak maximum with the reference result.
Use Analyze to inspect the width of the isolated peak. Record the selected background, the measured FWHM and the 2θ step of about 0.01313°.

Zoom near 67.5° and compare the close peaks with the isolated reflection. Use the standard to learn about instrument line shape. A raw width from this pattern is insufficient for a specimen crystallite-size result.
xrd.caption: Measured powder pattern with original counts, displayed without processing.

uvvis.title: Locating an absorption maximum
uvvis.provenance: Synthetic teaching data generated for SpectraSuite. A single Gaussian band on a constant absorbance background.
steps: Check that wavelength is in nm and the signal is absorbance.
Find the band maximum near 530 nm using the plot or data table.
Compare the peak with the expected raw absorbance of about 0.76. Keep the signal in absorbance for this exercise.
uvvis.expected: A maximum near 530 nm, with raw absorbance about 0.76.
uvvis.caption: Reference plot from the bundled synthetic dataset.

raman.title: Inspecting peaks on a sloping background
raman.provenance: Synthetic teaching data generated for SpectraSuite. Two Gaussian bands on a linear background.
steps: Locate the two bands near 520 and 1000 cm⁻¹.
Notice that the background increases with Raman shift. Compare the original trace with a baseline-corrected trace.
Compare heights only after choosing a consistent background and method.
raman.expected: Two prominent bands near 520 and 1000 cm⁻¹ above a rising background.
raman.caption: Reference plot from the bundled synthetic dataset.

general.title: Plotting a calibration line
general.provenance: Synthetic teaching data generated for SpectraSuite. An exact linear response with a small intercept.
steps: Check the X mapping for concentration and the Y mapping for absorbance.
Use Plot / refresh after changing mappings. Check the axis units and the intercept.
Compare the points with the straight-line response. Treat the bundled points as illustrative rather than an experimental calibration.
general.expected: A straight line from absorbance 0.02 at 0 mmol/L to 0.98 at 6 mmol/L.
general.caption: Reference plot from the bundled synthetic dataset.

plot3d.title: Visualizing a two-dimensional height field
plot3d.provenance: Synthetic teaching data generated for SpectraSuite. A sampled Gaussian height field.
steps: Check the X, Y and Z mappings and confirm all three axes are in millimetres.
Compare a point view with a surface view using the plot-type selector.
Rotate the view to see the central mound. Compare the height at the origin with the 5 mm expected value.
plot3d.expected: A symmetric mound with a height of 5 mm at the origin.
plot3d.caption: Reference plot from the bundled synthetic dataset.

xps.title: Inspecting a binding-energy peak
xps.provenance: Synthetic teaching data generated for SpectraSuite. A single Gaussian peak on a constant intensity background.
steps: Confirm binding energy in eV and intensity in arbitrary units.
Locate the peak near 285 eV and inspect the display axis direction.
Treat the energy as a synthetic peak position. A chemical assignment requires appropriate calibration and supporting evidence.
xps.expected: A peak near 285 eV. The synthetic data carry no chemical assignment.
xps.caption: Reference plot from the bundled synthetic dataset.

libs.title: Viewing two emission lines
libs.provenance: Synthetic teaching data generated for SpectraSuite. Two Gaussian emission lines on a constant background.
steps: Check wavelength in nm and intensity in arbitrary units.
Locate the two lines at about 450 and 462 nm. Compare their heights.
Treat these as unassigned synthetic lines. Confirm real assignments with reference lines, spectral resolution and possible interferences.
libs.expected: Lines near 450 and 462 nm, with the 450 nm line taller.
libs.caption: Reference plot from the bundled synthetic dataset.

fluid.title: Viewing a velocity field on a grid
fluid.provenance: Synthetic teaching data generated for SpectraSuite. An analytic parabolic speed profile sampled on a regular grid.
steps: Select Speed (m/s) as the plotted variable and inspect the color scale.
Choose Profile along Y, set the slice near the middle of X, then select Plot selected.
The profile peaks near the center of Y and reaches zero at both outer boundaries. Check the distance units before reporting a gradient.
fluid.expected: Speed is 1 m/s at Y = 0 and zero at the outer Y boundaries.
fluid.caption: Reference plot from the bundled synthetic dataset.
